title: Bonds Payable — Issuance at a Discount and Effective-Interest Amortization
scenario: On January 1, Year 1, Meridian Building Group issues $1,000,000 face value, 5-year bonds with a 6% annual stated rate; interest is paid each December 31. The market (effective) yield at issuance is 8%. Meridian uses the effective-interest method and the gross (separate discount account) presentation. Use the present-value factors and chart of accounts in the exhibits and round all amounts to the nearest dollar.

exhibits.label: Exhibit A — Bond terms and 8% present-value factors

tasks.prompt: Requirement 1 — Compute the issue price of the bonds and the discount on issuance.
tasks.explanation: Issue price = PV of coupons + PV of face at the 8% market yield = $60,000 × 3.992710 + $1,000,000 × 0.680583 = $239,563 + $680,583 = $920,146. Discount = $1,000,000 − $920,146 = $79,854. Bonds sell at a discount because the 6% stated rate is below the 8% market yield.

tasks.prompt: Requirement 2 — Record the January 1, Year 1 issuance entry using the gross method (account numbers from Exhibit B).
tasks.explanation: Dr Cash $920,146; Dr Discount on bonds payable $79,854; Cr Bonds payable $1,000,000 (face). The discount is a contra-liability that amortizes to interest expense over the term.

tasks.prompt: Requirement 3 — For Year 1, compute interest expense (effective-interest), the discount amortized, and the bonds' ending carrying value.
tasks.explanation: Interest expense = carrying value × market yield = $920,146 × 8% = $73,612. Cash coupon = $60,000, so discount amortized = $73,612 − $60,000 = $13,612. Ending carrying value = $920,146 + $13,612 = $933,758.

tasks.prompt: Requirement 4 — Record the December 31, Year 1 interest entry (effective-interest, gross method).
tasks.explanation: Dr Interest expense $73,612; Cr Discount on bonds payable $13,612 (amortization reduces the contra account, raising carrying value); Cr Cash $60,000 for the coupon.
